p1_findings.finding: The frozen M640 runner/wrapper use #!/usr/bin/env bash, so caller PATH resolves bash before the in-body readonly PATH. Bash also processes BASH_ENV before the body, and a hook can unset the evidence variables before the in-body test.
p1_findings.impact: Untrusted code can execute before host/GPU observations and receipts while leaving the body-visible startup variables empty.
p1_findings.required_fix: Use an absolute privileged Bash shebang, reseal every changed identity, and request a new fresh review.

p1_findings.finding: The three executable identities required by M640 were replaced before final rehash, while M640 contract/request still pin the old SHAs.
p1_findings.impact: There is no complete executable artifact set that the M640 authorization rule can admit.
p1_findings.required_fix: Freeze the new exact SHAs in a superseding contract and request; do not reuse M640 authorization.

p2_findings.finding: PYTHONPATH/PYTHONHOME/LD_PRELOAD/LD_LIBRARY_PATH and related runtime variables survive wrapper exec.
p2_findings.recommendation: Use env -i or an explicit allowlist and seal the effective environment/runtime content.

p2_findings.finding: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and related mapping are not cleared or sealed.
p2_findings.recommendation: Pin or clear mapping and record the effective PyTorch device identity.

authorization.next_action: Freeze the new absolute privileged-shebang generation in a superseding contract/request and run a fresh static hammer.
